Other Electrical and Electronic Goods Retailing

merger_description:
Rexel USA, Inc., a subsidiary of Rexel S.A. (together, along with its other global affiliates and subsidiaries, **Rexel**), has entered into an agreement to acquire Genuine Cable Group, LLC by acquiring:

* GCG Acquisition Holdings, LP by way of a merger.
* 100% of the issued share capital in AG CCA Blocker, Inc. and AG CCA Investment Corporation, Inc.
* 100% of the Class B Units in EIS Buyer, LLC.

Collectively, **GCG** (the **Acquisition**).

Rexel S.A. is a French distributor of electrical products, solutions, and services for the industrial, commercial, and residential markets. It operates in 17 countries and employs over 26,000 people worldwide. Rexel’s customers are wide ranging, including original equipment manufacturers, system integrators, utility companies, facility managers, hospitals, hotels, builders, electricians, and homeowners.

Rexel operates in Australia through an Australian subsidiary (**Rexel Australia**) using the Rexel, John R. Turk, Ideal Electrical, and Lear & Smith brands. It operates over 110 locations through these brands across Australia, providing electrical products to end customers.

GCG is a U.S.-based provider of wire, cable, and connectivity products. It also offers custom assembly, logistics, and wire manipulation services, and serves diverse sectors including communications, original equipment manufacturers, data centres, and renewable energy. Its brands include Allied Wire & Cable, Paige, and Olympic Wire & Cable Corp.

GCG does not distribute its products in the Australian market directly. Instead, some of its global distribution customers procure its specialty cables to on-distribute in Australia.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Rexel and
Genuine Cable Group in the supply of electrical cable
products in Australia
b. GCG has a small presence in Australia
c. there are alternative suppliers of electrical products
(including electrical cable products) in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
